Es el formato oficial del TCG: se juega: This is the official TCG format: it's played with all published cards and Konami's current banlist. It's the one covered by the top decks and tournaments in the other sections.
Main Deck de 40 a 60 cartas; Extra Deck: Main Deck of 40 to 60 cards; Extra Deck and Side Deck of up to 15.
Están todas las invocaciones: Fusión, Ri: All Summon types are available: Fusion, Ritual, Synchro, Xyz, Pendulum and Link, with the current zones (including the Extra Monster Zone).

Formato retro que se juega con las carta: Retro format played with the cards and banlist from spring 2010. It's named after the April 2010 Shonen Jump Championship in Edison (New Jersey), won by Jeff Jones with Quickdraw Plant. It's known for its variety of decks and its open deck building.
Banlist de marzo de 2010 (43 prohibidas,: March 2010 banlist (43 Forbidden, 70 Limited and 19 Semi-Limited).
Solo existen las invocaciones Normal, Ri: Only Normal, Ritual, Fusion and Synchro Summons exist: there are no Xyz, Pendulum or Link Summons, and no Extra Monster Zone (the extra zone for Links and Pendulums).
Los dos jugadores roban en el primer tur: Both players draw on the first turn (that rule was only removed with Pendulum, in 2014).
Las cartas se leen con el texto y las re: Cards are read with the text and official rulings of the era, not their current text.
El meta actual del formato lo dominan Bl: The format's current meta is dominated by Blackwing, HERO and the Frog variants; Lightsworn, Gladiator Beast, Vayu Turbo, Dragon, Fairy, Machina, Plant and Zombie are also played.
El primer formato de la era GX y uno de: The first format of the GX era and one of the most played retro formats. Its name comes from the Goat Control deck, one of the most successful of the time, although today the meta revolves around Chaos Turbo. It's a simple, interactive format: reading your opponent, bluffing and resource management matter most.
Banlist de abril de 2005 (17 prohibidas,: April 2005 banlist (17 Forbidden, 41 Limited and 15 Semi-Limited).
Las últimas expansiones del formato son: The format's latest expansions are Flaming Eternity and The Lost Millennium.
Hay Fusión y Ritual, pero no existen Sin: Fusion and Ritual exist, but there are no Synchro, Xyz, Pendulum or Link Summons.
Aparecen cartas nuevas de esa época como: New cards from that era show up, like Rescue Cat, Brain Control and Lightning Vortex. Chaos Turbo es el mazo de referencia; ta: Chaos Turbo is the benchmark deck; Warrior, Goat Control and other decks of the era are also played.
El último formato de la era Zexal y uno: The last format of the Zexal era and one of the most played retro formats. The name comes from three engines: Hand (hand), Artifact and Traptrix. It was the last format before Pendulum Monsters and before the first-turn draw was removed.
Banlist de abril de 2014 (77 prohibidas,: April 2014 banlist (77 Forbidden, 71 Limited and 14 Semi-Limited).
Hay Fusión, Ritual, Sincro y Xyz; no exi: Fusion, Ritual, Synchro and Xyz exist; there are no Pendulum or Link Summons.
Desde el formato Vegas se sumaron Dragon: Since the Vegas format, Dragons of Legend and Primal Origin were added: Traptrix Dionaea, Soul Charge, Sylvan support and the Artifact and Hand archetypes.
Se roba en el primer turno, como en Edis: You draw on the first turn, as in Edison and Goat.
El meta incluye Artifact Traptrix, Bujin: The meta includes Artifact Traptrix, Bujin, Geargia, Mermail and Spellbook, among others.
El OCG (Official Card Game) es la versió: The OCG (Official Card Game) is the version of the game sold in Japan and Asia. It shares most cards with the TCG, but its sets usually come out earlier and its banlist is different, which is why many people watch the OCG to anticipate what will happen in the TCG.
